console-sky.purpose: Console area program colour; login and mark tile.

players-green.purpose: Players area program colour; connection dot; log joins.

schedule-orange.purpose: Schedule area program colour; log WARN lines.

danger-red.purpose: Destructive actions, failures, RCON down, critical readouts.

on-area.purpose: Text and pictograms on solid program fields (light).

sunken-grey.purpose: Table headers, neutral pills, skeletons, dialog action bar (light).

rail-grey.purpose: Rail, phone tab bar, login ground (light).

on-area-dark.purpose: Text and pictograms on lifted program fields (dark).

navy-raised.purpose: Dark dialog surface (with line-strong border, no shadow).
navy-raised.note: Hard-coded literal in the dark .dialog rule, not a custom property.

display.purpose: Area name on its solid program field; 20px on phones.

numeral.purpose: Installed version on Updates; 20px on phones.

label.purpose: Uppercase condensed readout terms and table headers only.

log.purpose: Live log and command prompt only.

themes.light: Munich program on white: white ground, silver surface panels, white fields.
themes.dark: Lufthansa navy via prefers-color-scheme: navy ground, lighter navy panels, program hues lifted, on-area becomes deep navy.

shadows.name: overlay-dark
shadows.purpose: Defined as --shadow in dark; the dark dialog overrides it with box-shadow: none and a 1px line-strong border.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Focus indicator on fields and search (not elevation).

motion.name: state-tint
motion.purpose: Hover/selection tints on buttons, tabs, fields, rows, day chips.

motion.name: area-change
motion.purpose: Area-title field and band colour change on tab switch.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Dialog entrance (180ms), toast entrance (220ms), switch knob (180ms).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animation and transition durations collapse under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Health strip wraps under title; 20px gutters; schedule form two-up.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Panels stack to one column; console log 62dvh.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Bottom tab bar, 4x2 health grid, stacked tables with positioned labels, 16px inputs.

narrative.overview:
rconsole is run the way Otl Aicher ran the Munich '72 Games: a strict program of colours and geometric pictograms in which every place owns one hue and one sign, so the operator knows where they are and what state the server is in before reading a word. The five work areas (Console, Players, Backups, Schedule, Updates) are venues; each venue's colour lands on its signage (the solid area-title field), its rail tile, a 4px band under the top bar, and its primary actions. Everything else stays neutral so that colour keeps its meaning.

The density is an operator's: 14px body, 34px controls, hairline rules, tabular numerals in every readout and table. Surfaces are flat solid fills on 2px corners; depth exists only where something genuinely floats above the work (dialogs, toasts). Two themes share one program: the light theme is the Munich program on white with silver panels, the dark theme is Lufthansa navy with the same hues lifted for a dark ground.

The system rejects the category default of a grey-black dashboard with one neon accent and monospace everywhere. Monospace belongs to the log and the command prompt only; the UI speaks in Archivo, a Univers-like variable grotesk whose width axis carries hierarchy.
keyCharacteristics: One program colour per work area, applied as solid fields, never as gradients or glows.
Filled geometric pictograms on a 24-unit grid, 45/90 degree angles, round heads, for every area and action.
Flat 2px-cornered panels, hairline borders, shadows only on overlays.
Archivo variable for all UI, width axis used for signage (112%) and labels (92%); tabular numerals for every number.
Neutral health strip; colour appears only when something is off-nominal.

rules.name: The One Venue, One Colour Rule
rules.body: Each work area owns exactly one program colour and shows it in four places only: the solid area-title field, the active rail tile, the 4px band, and primary actions (plus in-area accents such as switches, selected segments, selected days, running/done jobs, `.own` pills, focus rings). No area borrows another's hue.

rules.name: The Red Means Danger Rule
rules.body: Red is reserved for destructive actions and failure or critical states. A red element is always a warning; nothing red is merely decorative.

rules.name: The Quiet Health Rule
rules.body: Health readouts are neutral ink when nominal. Off-nominal values gain the alert pictogram; "needs attention" stays ink with an ink-2 pictogram, "critical" turns the value red. The strip never borrows an area colour.

rules.name: The Hue-Free Countdown Rule
rules.body: The restart countdown banner is a solid ink field with ground-coloured text, deliberately outside the program so it reads as a server-wide event, not as any area.

rules.name: The Universal Signals Exception
rules.body: Two hues appear outside their area by design: log WARN lines stay schedule-orange (and joins players-green, commands console-sky) because they are log data, and the connection dot stays players-green as a universal state light.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by Archivo's width axis as much as by size: wide (105-112%) for signage and identity, normal for reading, condensed (92%) for data labels.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (readouts, counts, tables, versions, countdown) uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Only Overlays Float Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is above the page and will go away": dialogs and toasts. Anything resident in the layout is flat.

dos: Do route every area accent through `--area`, so the active venue's program colour drives fields, primary buttons, focus, switches and selected states automatically.
Do give every new area or action a filled geometric pictogram on the 24-unit grid (45/90 degree angles, round heads) and add it to the sprite.
Do keep panels flat: surface fill, 1px line border, 2px corners.
Do use tabular numerals for every changing number.
Do mark off-nominal states with the alert pictogram and, when critical or failed, danger red; leave nominal states neutral.
Do confirm destructive actions in the dialog with a red tile and a danger confirm button.
Do keep the light theme white ground / silver panels / white fields, and the dark theme Lufthansa navy with lifted program hues.
Do disable hover tints under `(hover: none)`; on phones use the bottom tab bar, the 2-row health grid and stacked tables with positioned labels.
donts: Don't use a second area's colour inside an area, or put a program colour on the health strip or countdown banner.
Don't use red for anything that is not destructive or failing.
Don't add glass, backdrop-filter, gradients, glows, or shadows on resident surfaces; only dialogs and toasts float, and the dark dialog uses a border instead.
Don't set UI text in monospace; mono is for the log, the prompt and codes.
Don't use stroked or outline icon sets or emoji; pictograms are filled geometry.
Don't round beyond 2px except for things that are round by nature (chips, counts, switches, dots).
